threads.body: The new Javadoc says "DO NOT USE OR OVERRIDE THIS METHOD" for `getDbOperationName`, but this interface is explicitly meant to be implemented by instrumentations and there are already in-repo implementations that override it to provide an explicit operation name (e.g., `InfluxDbAttributesGetter#getDbOperationName` at instrumentation/influxdb-2.4/...:35-39). This wording is misleading and discourages a supported/necessary use case when the operation name can’t be derived from SQL text.
threads.hunk:
@@ -23,8 +23,11 @@ public interface SqlClientAttributesGetter extends DbClientAttributesGetter { /** - * SqlClientAttributesExtractor will try to populate db.operation.name based on {@link - * #getRawQueryTexts(REQUEST)}, but this can be used to explicitly provide the operation name. + * DO NOT USE OR OVERRIDE THIS METHOD. + * + *

{@link SqlClientAttributesExtractor} will try to populate {@code db.operation.name} based on + * {@link #getRawQueryTexts(REQUEST)} when {@link + * SqlClientAttributesExtractorBuilder#setSingleOperationAndCollection(boolean)} is enabled.

threads.body: Similarly, the Javadoc for `getDbCollectionName` says "DO NOT USE OR OVERRIDE THIS METHOD" even though this is the extension point for instrumentations to provide an explicit `db.collection.name` (and `DbClientSpanNameExtractor` now prefers it over namespace for stable span names). The current wording is likely to confuse instrumentation authors and suggests they should not implement the attribute at all.
